payloads.text:
How to tell which objects in an AkashXDB database are RagBuckets or Ontology Views,
which SQL to use with each, and what lifecycle operations exist today. Every
statement below is taken from the product docs or from behaviour verified against a
live AkashXDB server; anything not supported is stated as not supported.
payloads.citation: Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views

payloads.text:
List the RagBuckets in the current database:

```sql
SHOW RAGBUCKET;
```

- The command is **singular**: `SHOW RAGBUCKET`. `SHOW RAGBUCKETS` (plural) is a
  **syntax error**.
- It returns one row per logical bucket. The bucket name is in the `ragbucket`
  column and the containing database in `database_name`. (Verified against a live
  AkashXDB server; the Superset AkashXDB engine spec relies on it.)
- The connection's current catalog/database scopes the listing, so run
  `SET CATALOG` / `USE` first if needed.

A RagBucket is a **document corpus, not a table**. Creating one also creates
physical tables named after the bucket — `<bucket>_metadata`, `<bucket>_raw_files`,
`<bucket>_chunks` and `<bucket>_intermediate_table` (plus
`<bucket>_sharepoint_changes` for SharePoint buckets). Those are internal storage,
so `SHOW TABLES` lists them but cannot tell you which bucket they belong to — use
`SHOW RAGBUCKET` to identify the buckets themselves.
payloads.citation: Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Identify RagBuckets (SHOW RAGBUCKET)

payloads.text:
List the Ontology Views in the current database:

```sql
SHOW ONTOLOGY VIEWS;
```

- The view name is in the `view_name` column and the containing database in
  `database_name`.
- An Ontology View is backed by a real table, so it also appears in `SHOW TABLES`
  as an ordinary base table — **`SHOW TABLES` cannot distinguish an Ontology View
  from a normal table.** Use `SHOW ONTOLOGY VIEWS`.
payloads.citation: Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Identify Ontology Views (SHOW ONTOLOGY VIEWS)

payloads.text:
| Object | How to query it |
|---|---|
| Table | Normal `SELECT`. |
| Ontology View | Normal `SELECT`; filter `WHERE status = 'done'` for rows whose extraction finished, e.g. `SELECT * FROM <view> WHERE status = 'done';` |
| RagBucket | `ASK '<natural-language question>' ON <bucket>` (managed retrieval). Never `SELECT` from the bucket name — it has no columns. |

Use `CREATE RAGBUCKET` — see **RagBucket > SQL Syntax** for the full statement and
properties, and **Quick-Start Examples** for complete Azure and SharePoint pathways.

```sql
CREATE RAGBUCKET <bucket_name> FROM 's3://<user-bucket>/<path>/'
PROPERTIES (
  "aws.s3.access_key" = "...",
  "aws.s3.secret_key" = "...",
  "aws.s3.region" = "us-east-1",
  "llm_provider" = "grok",
  "llm_model" = "grok-4-fast",
  "embedding_provider" = "openai",
  "embedding_model" = "text-embedding-3-small"
);
```
payloads.citation: Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Create a RagBucket

payloads.text:
See **Ontology > SQL Syntax**. The source clause takes two forms:

- `ON COLUMN <table>.<column>` and `ON LINKS <table>.<column>` — name the table **and**
  the column holding the text or links.
- `ON RAGBUCKET <bucket>` — the **bare bucket name only**, no `.column`; the source
  text is taken automatically from the bucket's `_raw_files.raw_text`.

```sql
CREATE ONTOLOGY VIEW az_demo_ont (
    Summary TEXT AS 'Summarize the document'
)
ON RAGBUCKET az_demo
USING ''
PROPERTIES (
    "rate_limit"     = "5",
    "time_interval"  = "30 SECOND",
    "llm_provider"   = "openai",
    "llm_model"      = "gpt-4o-mini"
);
```
payloads.citation: Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Identify and Manage RagBuckets and Ontology Views > Create an Ontology View (ON COLUMN, ON LINKS, ON RAGBUCKET)

payloads.text:
There is **no `DROP RAGBUCKET` and no `ALTER RAGBUCKET` statement** — the grammar only
implements `CREATE RAGBUCKET` (RagBucket SharePoint design, gap G8). Do not write
either statement; it will fail.

To remove a RagBucket, drop its scheduled tasks and tables manually with the
documented **Cleanup template** below. After cleanup the bucket **name cannot be
reused** — the `RagBucketMgr` entry persists — so pick a new name when you recreate it.

For SharePoint-backed Ontology Views, the soft-delete cascade is enabled with:

```sql
REFRESH ONTOLOGY VIEW WITH ASYNC MODE ON;
```

This enables the `OntologyRefreshDaemon`. It **resets when the FE restarts**, so re-run

payloads.text: Ontology is an AI-powered structured data extraction system. It takes unstructured text (or links/files) and extracts structured fields using LLMs, storing the results in a queryable table with typed columns.
payloads.citation: Ontology > Ontology > Overview

payloads.text:
```sql
CREATE ONTOLOGY VIEW <view_name>
  (<column_name> <type> AS '<extraction_instruction>', ...)
  ON COLUMN|LINKS|RAGBUCKET <table>.<column>
  USING '<global_prompt>'
  PROPERTIES (
    "rate_limit" = "10",
    "time_interval" = "10",
    "llm_provider" = "grok",
    "llm_model" = "grok-4-fast"
    -- "has_acl" = "true"   -- optional; usually auto-derived (see below)
  );
```
payloads.citation: Ontology > Ontology > SQL Syntax

payloads.text:
- **COLUMN** - Base column contains raw text. LLM processes text directly.
- **LINKS** - Base column contains URIs/URLs. UDF fetches content from the URL (supports S3 with AWS credentials).
- **RAGBUCKET** - Automatically uses the `_raw_files` table from a ragbucket, extracting from `raw_text` with S3 HTTPS URL conversion.
payloads.citation: Ontology > Ontology > SQL Syntax > Source Types

payloads.text:
Controls per-row ACL columns and query-time row-level security. The PROPERTY is optional — the view derives it from the source:

- **ON RAGBUCKET** → reads `bucket.hasAcl` (SharePoint defaults to `true`; S3/Azure to `false`).
- **ON COLUMN / ON LINKS** → `true` only when the base table has all 5 `acl_*` columns + `last_modified_at` + `refreshed_at`.
- Explicit `has_acl = "true"` is rejected if the source can't provide ACL data.
- Explicit `has_acl = "false"` is respected (single-tenant opt-out).
payloads.citation: Ontology > Ontology > SQL Syntax > `has_acl` (auto-derived)

payloads.text:
The four ways `bucket.has_acl` and `view.has_acl` can pair:

| Bucket | View | What happens | Useful? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `true` | `true` | View carries 5 ACL cols + 2 timestamp cols. ACL refresh runs on changes. RLS filters rows at query time. | ✓ Standard SharePoint flow. |
| `true` | `false` | View has **no** ACL cols. Preseed skips `acl_*`. No RLS — anyone with `SELECT` on the view sees every row. | Allowed; legit use cases include admin-only views and aggregated/public summaries. Risky if set by mistake — the LLM extractions of restricted files become queryable by everyone. |
| `false` | `true` | Bucket's `_raw_files` has no ACL columns to read. Preseed would reference `r.acl_users` and fail. | ✗ **Rejected at CREATE time** with a clear error. |
| `false` | `false` | No ACL on either side. Standard non-SharePoint flow. | ✓ Standard S3/Azure flow. |

**Foot-gun warning for case 2** (`bucket=true`, `view=false`): the downgrade is silent — only an INFO log line records the mismatch (`Ontology view has_acl resolved: false (derived=true, property=false)`). If you genuinely want a non-RLS view over ACL'd data, set the PROPERTY explicitly so it's intentional, not a typo.

payloads.text: Scope: this doc covers Ontology Views whose source path leads back to **object storage** — i.e. `ON COLUMN` / `ON LINKS` over a regular table without ACL columns, or `ON RAGBUCKET` over an S3/MinIO/Azure-backed RagBucket. SharePoint-specific behavior (ACL columns, soft-delete cascade, Tier-3 refresh) is **excluded** here; that lives in [ONTOLOGY.md](ONTOLOGY.md) and the SharePoint docs.
payloads.citation: Ontology View (Object Storage Sources) > Ontology View (Object Storage Sources)

payloads.text:
An Ontology View is a managed LLM-extraction pipeline. From a single `CREATE ONTOLOGY VIEW` statement, the engine:

1. Creates **one table** in your database with: a copy of the source text, the columns you declared, bookkeeping columns for task state, and (for `ON RAGBUCKET`) two URL columns.
2. Seeds that table with one row per source row, marked `status='READY'`.
3. Schedules **three recurring tasks** that submit extraction requests to Redis, poll status, and clean up.

The external worker pulls each request from Redis, runs the LLM with your global prompt + per-column instructions, returns a JSON object, and the status task fans that JSON out into the typed columns you declared.
payloads.citation: Ontology View (Object Storage Sources) > Ontology View (Object Storage Sources) > What is an Ontology View?

payloads.text:
```sql
CREATE ONTOLOGY VIEW <view_name>
  (<column_name> <type> AS '<extraction_instruction>', ...)
  ON COLUMN|LINKS|RAGBUCKET <db>.<table>.<column>
  USING '<global_prompt>'
  PROPERTIES (
    "rate_limit"        = "10",
    "time_interval"     = "10",
    "llm_provider"      = "grok",
    "llm_model"         = "grok-4-fast"
    -- optional: "batch_mode" = "true", "batch_limit" = "10"
    -- optional (LINKS only): "aws.access.key" / "aws.secret.key" / "storage_volume"
  );
```
payloads.citation: Ontology View (Object Storage Sources) > Ontology View (Object Storage Sources) > SQL Syntax

payloads.text:
| Mode | Source column contains | What the worker does |
|---|---|---|
| `ON COLUMN` | Raw text | Sends the text straight to the LLM |
| `ON LINKS` | URL or URI | Fetches the URL (S3 supported via AWS creds), then LLM |
| `ON RAGBUCKET` | (auto: uses the ragbucket's `_raw_files.raw_text`) | LLM on `raw_text`; also converts `s3://` → HTTPS |

For object-storage sources, `has_acl` resolves to `false` automatically — for `ON RAGBUCKET` because the underlying S3/Azure bucket has `hasAcl=false`, and for `ON COLUMN`/`ON LINKS` because regular tables don't carry the 5 `acl_*` columns + 2 timestamp columns the executor looks for. Explicit `has_acl=true` is rejected at CREATE time if the source can't supply ACL data.

payloads.text:
At CREATE time, one row is inserted per source row.

**For `ON RAGBUCKET`** ([OntologyViewExecutor.java:494-521](../fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/qe/OntologyViewExecutor.java#L494-L521)):

```sql
INSERT INTO <view> (_base_pk, <base_col>, file_url, https_url, request_id, status)
SELECT <pk>, <base_col>, file_url,
       REPLACE(CONCAT('https://', SPLIT_PART(file_url,'/',3),
                      '.s3.<aws.s3.region>.amazonaws.com/', ...), ' ', '+') AS https_url,
       uuid(), 'READY'
FROM <base_db>.<base_table>;
```

**For `ON COLUMN` / `ON LINKS`** ([OntologyViewExecutor.java:523-536](../fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/qe/OntologyViewExecutor.java#L523-L536)):

```sql
INSERT INTO <view> (_base_pk, <base_col>, request_id, status)
SELECT <pk>, <base_col>, uuid(), 'READY'
FROM <base_db>.<base_table>;
```

User-defined columns remain NULL until the status task fills them in. New rows added to the base table later are picked up by the same scheduled-tasks loop.

payloads.text:
Three tasks ([OntologyViewExecutor.java:623, 723, 754](../fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/qe/OntologyViewExecutor.java#L623)):

| Task name | Interval | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ont_submit_<db>_<table>` | `time_interval` property | Picks `status='READY'` rows (up to `rate_limit`), calls `ontology_redis_submit_udf()` with prompt + schema + LLM config + AWS creds, updates `status` / `message` / `error` |
| `ont_status_<db>_<table>` | 15 SECOND | Polls Redis for non-terminal rows via `ontology_redis_status_udf()`, extracts typed fields from the result JSON into your user columns using `get_json_string()` / `get_json_int()` / `get_json_double()` / `get_json_bool()` |
| `ont_dk_<db>_<table>` | 60 SECOND | For `status='done'` rows, calls `ontology_redis_dk_udf()` to drop the Redis hash and resets `retry` to 0 |

Both `<db>` and `<table>` in task names are sanitized — non-alphanumeric characters become underscores.

> Note: the submit interval has **no default in code** — `time_interval` (and `rate_limit`) come straight from your PROPERTIES with no fallback. Omitting them will produce an invalid `SCHEDULE EVERY` clause at CREATE time. [Likely] required in practice.

payloads.text:
The worker consumes tasks from `ragbucket_stream` and processes documents:

1. **Download** - Fetches the file from the user's S3 using download credentials
2. **Parse** - Extracts text from PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD files
3. **Semantic Sectioning** - Identifies logical document structure using LLM
4. **Chunking** - Splits into chunks with configurable size
5. **Embedding** - Generates vector embeddings for each chunk (768 dimensions)
6. **Auto-Context** - Generates document and section summaries
7. **Parquet Output** - Serializes chunks + vectors into Parquet format
8. **Upload** - Uploads Parquet to the dsRAG S3 path

The intermediate Parquet table then picks up the output, and the chunk insert task loads it into the chunks table.

- **`check_redis_task_status()`** - Queries Redis hash, returns full status JSON. Strips sensitive credentials before returning.

payloads.text:
`dest_url` is the **base** sink path. Each `CREATE RAGBUCKET <name>` writes parquet under `<base>/<name>/...` (the bucket's prefix is the lowercased ragbucket name). So `sp_test` with `dest_url = s3://akashx-ragbucket/` lands at `s3://akashx-ragbucket/sp_test/Doc1.parquet`. Same shape applies for Azure: `wasbs://desttest@myaccount.../sp_test/Doc1.parquet`.

payloads.text:
Searches the ragbucket's chunks table using HNSW vector index with cosine similarity.

```sql
WITH topk AS (
    SELECT *, cosine_similarity(vector, @qv) AS score
    FROM <bucket>_chunks
    WHERE cosine_similarity(vector, @qv) > threshold
    ORDER BY score DESC
    LIMIT 200
)
```

- Uses the HNSW index on the `vector` column (768 dimensions)
- Retrieves the top 200 most semantically similar chunks

Anything ACL-, drive-item-, or soft-delete-related is SharePoint-only and not present in the tables described here.

payloads.text:
A RagBucket is a managed ingestion + retrieval pipeline pointed at an object-storage path. From a single `CREATE RAGBUCKET` statement, the engine:

1. Stands up four tables under the current database — one for metadata, one to track each source file, one for chunk+vector storage, and one external Parquet table that bridges in worker output.
2. Schedules five recurring tasks that continuously scan the source path, dispatch new files to an external worker (dsRAG) via Redis, monitor status, load processed chunks, and clean up.
3. Persists the bucket definition through `EditLog` so it survives FE restarts.

Once chunks are loaded, the bucket is queryable two ways: directly via SQL (e.g. `cosine_similarity(vector, …)`) and through the natural-language `PROMPT` / `ASK` syntax described at the bottom of [RAGBUCKET.md](RAGBUCKET.md).

payloads.text:
```sql
CREATE RAGBUCKET <bucket_name> FROM '<source-url>'
PROPERTIES (
  -- source credentials (one of these two groups)
  -- ...inline (S3/MinIO):
  "aws.s3.access_key" = "...",
  "aws.s3.secret_key" = "...",
  "aws.s3.region"     = "us-east-1",
  -- ...or a storage volume reference:
  -- "storage_volume" = "my_source_volume",

  -- LLM + embedding
  "llm_provider"       = "grok",
  "llm_model"          = "grok-4-fast",
  "embedding_provider" = "openai",
  "embedding_model"    = "text-embedding-3-small",

  -- parquet sink (must be set together, or both omitted for legacy fallback)
  "dest_storage_volume" = "my_dest_volume",
  "dest_url"            = "s3://my-ragbucket-sink/"
);
```

Accepted source URL schemes (verified in [RagBucketExecutor.java:148-156](../fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/qe/RagBucketExecutor.java#L148-L156)):

| Scheme | Source |
|---|---|
| `s3://...` | AWS S3 / MinIO / any S3-compatible |
| `wasbs://...` or `azblob://...` | Azure Blob Storage |

`has_acl=true` is explicitly **rejected** for these sources — it's a SharePoint-only feature ([RagBucketExecutor.java:164-168](../fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/qe/RagBucketExecutor.java#L164-L168)).

payloads.text:
SharePoint file processing is a two-system pipeline. The **external crawler** (`akashx-sharepoint-sync`) walks SharePoint via Microsoft Graph and writes file metadata + ACL into the central catalog `sharepoint_meta.sys_sharepoint_files`. **RagBucket** then reads from that catalog for its chunks/embeddings pipeline, and **Ontology View** reads from RagBucket (or from a user base table populated by `SP_FILES()`) to run LLM extraction.

```
SharePoint
   ↓ (Microsoft Graph API)
[crawler daemon — external Python process]
   ↓ writes
sharepoint_meta.sys_sharepoint_files   (per-file row + ACL, partitioned by site_id)
   ↓ (read by both consumers)
   ├──→ RagBucket stage task  →  _raw_files (with ACL)  →  chunks + HNSW
   └──→ SP_FILES() sync rule  →  user base table       →  Ontology View
```

The same catalog feeds both consumer paths. RagBucket-backed ontology views inherit ACL columns; LINKS- and COLUMN-mode views inherit them via the user's sync rule.

payloads.text:
**Register a SharePoint site** (one-time, per site):
```sql
CREATE SHAREPOINT_SITE demosite
PROPERTIES (
    "site_url"   = "https://akashxsharepoint.sharepoint.com/sites/DemoSite",
    "full_cron"  = "0 2 * * *",
    "delta_cron" = "5 0-1,3-23 * * *"
);
```

**Path format for RagBucket logical path:**
```
sharepoint://<site_id>/
```
The `<site_id>` matches the registered site name above. RagBucket binds to the site by id, not by URL parsing.

**Minimal `CREATE RAGBUCKET`:**
```sql
CREATE RAGBUCKET sp_testrag
FROM 'sharepoint://demosite/'
PROPERTIES (
  'storage_volume'      = 'sp_creds',
  'source_site_id'      = 'demosite',
  'metadata_interval'   = '300 SECOND',
  'rate_limit'          = '5',
  'dest_storage_volume' = 'minio_dest',
  'dest_url'            = 's3://akashx-ragbucket/'
  -- 'has_acl' = 'false'   -- optional; defaults 'true' for SharePoint
);
```

payloads.text:
**Notes:**
- `source_site_id` is required and validated at create time. Register the site first.
- `has_acl` defaults: `true` for SharePoint, `false` for S3/Azure. Explicit `true` on non-SharePoint is rejected. `ON RAGBUCKET` ontology views auto-derive from the bucket.
- `dest_storage_volume` + `dest_url` together specify where parquet chunks land. See [RAGBUCKET.md → Destination](RAGBUCKET.md#destination-where-dsrag-writes-parquet-chunks) for S3 / MinIO / Azure setup.

**Per-bucket tables created:**

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `<prefix>_raw_files` | File inventory + status. **16 cols on S3/Azure; 17 with SharePoint `has_acl=false` (adds `drive_item_id`); 24 with SharePoint `has_acl=true` (adds 5 ACL cols + `last_modified_at` + `refreshed_at`).** |
| `<prefix>_sharepoint_changes` | Staging buffer; PK on `drive_item_id` |
| `<prefix>_metadata`, `<prefix>_chunks`, `<prefix>_intermediate_table` | Same as S3/Azure ragbuckets |

payloads.text:
**Per-bucket scan tasks (SharePoint-specific):**
- `<prefix>_sharepoint_stage` — reads `sys_sharepoint_files` for this site_id, anti-joins for deletes, writes staging
- `<prefix>_sharepoint_apply_new` — INSERTs new files into `_raw_files` with ACL
- `<prefix>_sharepoint_apply_modify` — UPDATEs on watermark; handles renames; refreshes ACL (COALESCE-guarded)
- `<prefix>_sharepoint_apply_delete` — soft-deletes via `deleted_at = NOW()`

For the why behind this shape, see [design §1 Pipeline overview](RAGBUCKET_SHAREPOINT_DESIGN.md#1-pipeline-overview).

payloads.text: The catalog table `sharepoint_meta.sys_sharepoint_files` is the single source of truth for "what files exist on SharePoint and who can see them." It's populated by the external crawler (`akashx-sharepoint-sync`) which talks to Microsoft Graph and writes one row per file per site. RagBucket reads from this catalog — it does NOT walk Graph itself.
payloads.citation: SharePoint RagBucket — Design > SharePoint RagBucket — Design > 1. Pipeline overview

payloads.text:
```
                              ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                              │ akashx-sharepoint-sync (external)│
                              │   walks Graph, writes catalog    │
                              └────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                               ▼
                       sharepoint_meta.sys_sharepoint_files
                       (per-site partition, per-file row, ACL columns,
                        refreshed_at + last_modified_at timestamps)
                                               │
                ┌──────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
                │ <prefix>_sharepoint_stage  (every metadata_interval)  │
                │   SELECT FROM sys_sharepoint_files WHERE site_id=…    │
                │   UNION ALL  anti-join for deletes                    │
                │   →  upserts _sharepoint_changes (PK drive_item_id)   │
                └────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                             │
                ┌────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┐
                ▼                            ▼                        ▼
   <prefix>_sharepoint_apply_new   apply_modify              apply_delete
   INSERT new rows + ACL           UPDATE on watermark       SET deleted_at=NOW()
   (drive_item_id NOT IN           (mod_time newer);         (matched by
   _raw_files)                     COALESCE-refresh ACL      drive_item_id)
```
payloads.citation: SharePoint RagBucket — Design > SharePoint RagBucket — Design > 1. Pipeline overview

payloads.text:
The stage task uses a race-free watermark: it filters `sys_sharepoint_files` by `refreshed_at > MAX(source_refreshed_at)` already in staging. The watermark uses the catalog's own clock, so the bucket DB's `NOW()` doesn't need to be aligned with the crawler's clock.

The two halves of the stage task (upsert + delete) are UNION ALL'd into one INSERT so a single SUBMIT TASK fires both per tick. The PRIMARY KEY on `<prefix>_sharepoint_changes(drive_item_id)` means re-staging the same drive_item_id replaces the previous staging row in place.

payloads.text:
When `apply_delete` sets `_raw_files.deleted_at`, two downstream effects fire from **`OntologyRefreshDaemon`** (every 30s tick):

- **Chunks cleanup** — hard-DELETE rows in `<prefix>_chunks` for tombstoned files. HNSW gets tombstones; segment compaction reclaims space. The `chunk_insert` task has a matching `AND r.deleted_at IS NULL` guard so deleted chunks aren't re-inserted from parquet.
- **Ontology view cascade** — partial-INSERT sets `deleted_at` on view rows whose `_base_pk` matches a tombstoned `_raw_files` row. Only runs for `ON RAGBUCKET` views backed by a SharePoint bucket. View keeps the LLM extraction for audit; query-side filtering on `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` hides them.

Both are idempotent. The daemon executes via `StmtExecutor` (not `SUBMIT TASK`, which rejects `DELETE`). The chunks step uses a two-step `SELECT` + `DELETE WHERE ... IN (literal list)` pattern because StarRocks DELETE on DUPLICATE KEY tables rejects subqueries inside IN.

S3/Azure buckets have no `deleted_at` column and no `apply_delete` task — the cascade is a no-op.

**File discovery (external crawler daemon):**
- Runs as a long-running process outside akashxdb (`sharepoint-crawler-daemon`)

**File download (dsRAG worker):**
- Triggered by the standard ragbucket task pipeline → worker → `/extract_row_level_chunks_vectors`

- Calls FE at `host.docker.internal:8030` (cross-container) for credential resolution
- 5-minute per-worker cache via `credential_resolver.py`

- `ALTER STORAGE VOLUME sp_creds SET ...`
- Crawler picks up new creds on its next credential refresh cycle (configurable)
- Download picks up new creds within 5 minutes (worker cache TTL)
- For immediate effect, restart the crawler container and the dsRAG worker

payloads.text:
SharePoint rows in `_raw_files` carry a `drive_item_id` column populated from Graph's `item_id`. apply-modify and apply-delete match on this column rather than on `file_url`, because:

- `file_url` embeds the filename. On rename, `file_url` changes; `item_id` is stable.
- Graph's delete payload contains only `item_id` (no `name`, no `lastModifiedDateTime`), so `file_url` isn't reconstructable for tombstones.

For S3/Azure, `drive_item_id` is NULL — those sources continue to use `file_url` as their natural identity. The column is nullable and the existing S3/Azure scan-task INSERT doesn't reference it, so behavior on those sources is unchanged.

payloads.text: `apply-modify` only fires when `c.modification_time > r.modification_time`. Without this filter every tick would re-mark already-completed files as `READY` and the worker would loop forever. After the worker reprocesses, the row's `modification_time` matches the staging row, comparisons return false, ticks become noops.

payloads.text:
The stage task emits `change_type='upserted'` for catalog rows whose `refreshed_at` is newer than what's already staged, and `change_type='deleted'` for `_raw_files` rows that no longer appear in the catalog (anti-join). Apply tasks split:
- **apply-new:** `change_type='upserted' AND drive_item_id NOT IN _raw_files`
- **apply-modify:** `change_type='upserted' AND watermark says newer`
- **apply-delete:** `change_type='deleted'`

apply-new and apply-modify intentionally have overlapping `WHERE` clauses so the order of task execution within a tick doesn't matter — each is idempotent.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | New file added | ✅ | apply-new picks it up |
| 2 | Modified file (same id, edited content) | ✅ | apply-modify resets `status=READY`; bumps `r.modification_time` |
| 3 | Deleted file | ✅ | matched by `drive_item_id`; soft-deleted via `status=deleted` |
| 4 | Renamed file (same id, new filename) | ✅ | apply-modify updates `file_url` + `file_name` in place |

| 6 | Resurrection (delete + re-add with same id) | ✅ | apply-modify sees newer mod-time, resets `status` |
| 7 | Moved out of watched folder | 🐛 G1 | scope filter drops the row before staging — `_raw_files` stays stale |
| 8 | Moved into watched folder | ✅ | item appears as a new id in scope; apply-new inserts |

payloads.text:
- **Single source of truth.** `sharepoint_meta.sys_sharepoint_files` is written by one process (the external crawler) and read by every consumer (RagBucket, SP_FILES, ontology views). One walk of Graph per site regardless of how many ragbuckets reference it.
- **ACL flows for free.** The crawler populates the five ACL columns once per file; every consumer inherits them, enabling RLS on RagBucket-backed and SP_FILES-backed ontology views uniformly.
- **Bounded I/O.** Staging is one row per file (PK on `drive_item_id`); the catalog is partitioned by site_id so per-site lifecycle is isolated.
- **Bucket-local state stays contained.** All bucket-local tables live in the bucket DB, so dropping the database (or manually dropping the tables) removes them. The shared catalog is untouched.
- **No bucket-local cursor.** No `_sharepoint_state` to manage, no per-bucket delta replay. The race-free watermark uses `refreshed_at` from the catalog directly.
payloads.citation: SharePoint RagBucket — Design > SharePoint RagBucket — Design > 8. Pros & Cons > 8.1 Pros

payloads.text:
- **Site must be registered before bucket create.** Adds a step compared to S3/Azure, but the validation surfaces typos at create time rather than at first task tick.
- **`file_url` is no longer immutable on a SharePoint row.** apply-modify can change it on rename. Any downstream consumer that caches `file_url` needs to tolerate this.
- **More tasks per bucket.** SharePoint creates 4 scan-related tasks instead of 1. Each is cheap, but log volume increases. Drift the cadence longer if it's noisy.
- **Crawler is a separate deploy unit.** A second container/process must be running for SharePoint to work. Compared to the old in-process UDTF, this is more moving parts but also clean ownership boundaries.
- **Mixed-source queries.** Anything that does `WHERE drive_item_id = ...` on `_raw_files` silently drops S3/Azure rows. Fine since `drive_item_id` is SharePoint-only by design.

SharePoint OAuth2 client credentials are stored in a StarRocks Storage Volume of type `ADLS2`. The ADLS2 type is reused because it carries the same `tenant_id` / `client_id` / `client_secret` schema needed for the Graph API client-credentials flow — only the OAuth2 scope at token-request time differs.

CREATE STORAGE VOLUME sp_creds
TYPE = ADLS2
LOCATIONS = ("adls2://dummy")
PROPERTIES (
  "azure.adls2.oauth2_tenant_id"     = "<your-tenant-id>",

| Aspect | S3 | Azure Blob | SharePoint |

| `FROM` path | `s3://bucket/path` | `wasbs://container@account/path` | `sharepoint://<site_id>/` |
| Site registration | n/a | n/a | `CREATE SHAREPOINT_SITE` first; bucket binds to `source_site_id` |
| File discovery | `FILES()` table function (BE) | `FILES()` table function (BE) | External crawler daemon writes `sys_sharepoint_files`; bucket stage task reads from there |
| Listing strategy | Full listing per scan + `WHERE NOT IN` dedupe | Same as S3 | Catalog-backed; per-tick watermark on `refreshed_at`; anti-join for deletes |
| Identity key | `file_url` | `file_url` | `drive_item_id` (Graph driveItem.id) |
| ACL + timestamps on `_raw_files` | n/a | n/a | 5 ACL cols + `last_modified_at` + `refreshed_at`, added only when `has_acl=true` |
| `has_acl` default | `false` (explicit `true` rejected) | `false` (explicit `true` rejected) | `true` (ontology views auto-derive) |
| Storage volume | Optional | Optional | **Required** (must be ADLS2; consumed by crawler + worker) |
| Download backend | `S3Storage` | `AzureBlobStorage` | `SharePointStorage` |
| URL scheme | `s3://bucket/key` | `wasbs://container@account/blob` | `sharepoint://driveId/driveItemId/filename` |
| Modify detection | None — re-listed each scan | None | Watermark on `modification_time` (apply-modify) |
| Delete handling | Implicit (file disappears from listing) | Same | Explicit anti-join in stage task; soft-delete via `deleted_at = NOW()` (separate column from `status`, which is the Redis task lifecycle) |

payloads.text:
When SharePoint deletes a file, we need to:
1. Mark it as deleted in the ragbucket without losing the row (for audit / replay).
2. Stop returning its chunks from vector search.
3. Stop returning its rows from any ontology view built on the bucket.

This is **SharePoint-only**. S3 and Azure ragbuckets don't have a delete signal — files just stop showing up in the listing — so the cascade is a no-op there.
payloads.citation: Soft Delete (SharePoint) > Soft Delete (SharePoint)

payloads.text:
| Layer | Column | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| `<bucket>_raw_files` | `deleted_at DATETIME` (NULL = alive) | `<bucket>_sharepoint_apply_delete` task |
| `<bucket>_chunks` | (no column — rows are hard-deleted) | `OntologyRefreshDaemon` |
| Ontology view backing table | `deleted_at DATETIME` (NULL = alive) | `OntologyRefreshDaemon` |

`deleted_at` is **separate from `status`**. `status` tracks the Redis task lifecycle (`READY` / `submitted` / `completed` / `error`). Don't conflate them.
payloads.citation: Soft Delete (SharePoint) > Soft Delete (SharePoint) > Where the signal lives

payloads.text:
```
SharePoint file deleted
        │
        ▼  (crawler removes row from sys_sharepoint_files)
<bucket>_sharepoint_stage task
        │  picks up missing drive_item_id via anti-join → emits change_type='deleted'
        ▼
<bucket>_sharepoint_apply_delete task
        │  sets _raw_files.deleted_at = NOW()
        ▼
OntologyRefreshDaemon (every 30s)
        ├─► hard-DELETE rows in <bucket>_chunks for the deleted file
        │   (HNSW index gets tombstones; segment compaction reclaims space)
        │
        └─► partial-INSERT to set ontology_view.deleted_at = NOW()
            for every view row whose _base_pk matches a tombstoned _raw_files row
```

Each step is idempotent. The daemon doesn't track what it's already cleaned — it just re-runs the same SQL every tick. After the first run, follow-up ticks find nothing to do.
payloads.citation: Soft Delete (SharePoint) > Soft Delete (SharePoint) > End-to-end flow

payloads.text: StarRocks `SUBMIT TASK` rejects `UPDATE` and `DELETE` in the task body — only `INSERT`, `CTAS`, and `DATACACHE SELECT` are accepted. The daemon executes via `StmtExecutor` directly, which has no such restriction.
payloads.citation: Soft Delete (SharePoint) > Soft Delete (SharePoint) > Why the daemon, not a SUBMIT TASK

payloads.text:
**`<bucket>_raw_files.deleted_at`** — only added when the source is SharePoint (`bucket.isSharepoint() = true`). S3/Azure buckets don't get the column at all.

**Ontology view `deleted_at`** — only added when the view is `ON RAGBUCKET <bucket>` and the bucket is SharePoint. `ON LINKS` / `ON COLUMN` views don't get the column (their base tables have no `deleted_at` to cascade from).

**`<bucket>_chunks`** — no `deleted_at` column. Rows are hard-deleted; the file_name in the deletion list comes from `_raw_files.deleted_at IS NOT NULL`. The `<bucket>_chunk_insert` task has a matching `AND r.deleted_at IS NULL` guard so chunks for tombstoned files aren't re-inserted from parquet.
payloads.citation: Soft Delete (SharePoint) > Soft Delete (SharePoint) > Schema gating

payloads.text:
[OntologyRefreshDaemon.java](../fe/fe-core/src/main/java/com/starrocks/qe/OntologyRefreshDaemon.java) — two methods called per tick before the existing PAUSED/ACTIVE handling:

```java
runChunksDeleteCascade();   // hard-deletes chunks for tombstoned files
runOvDeleteCascade(meta);   // partial-INSERTs deleted_at on view rows
```

The chunks cascade uses a **two-step** pattern because StarRocks DELETE on DUPLICATE KEY tables rejects subqueries in IN predicates ("Child of in predicate should be value"):

```java
// Step 1: read deleted file_names
SELECT DISTINCT file_name FROM <bucket>_raw_files WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL;

// Step 2: DELETE with inline literal IN-list
DELETE FROM <bucket>_chunks WHERE file_name IN ('Doc1.pdf', 'Doc2.pdf', ...);
```

Single quotes in file names are escaped.

The OV cascade is a single partial-INSERT upsert on the PRIMARY KEY:

```sql
INSERT INTO <view> (id, deleted_at)
SELECT v.id, NOW()
FROM <view> v
JOIN <bucket>_raw_files r ON v._base_pk = r.id
WHERE r.deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND v.deleted_at IS NULL;
```

The `v.deleted_at IS NULL` guard makes it idempotent.
